warnings.headline: A spell of strong south to south-westerly winds may cause some disruption during Monday evening and the early hours of Tuesday.
warnings.description:
South to south-westerly winds will increase from the west during Monday evening with gusts of 45-50 mph inland and 60-65 mph along exposed coasts and over high ground. The strong winds will be accompanied by heavy rain at times.

Winds will then ease from the west during the early hours, before increasing again across northern parts of the UK early on Tuesday morning.
impacts: It’s likely that some coastal routes, sea fronts and coastal communities will be affected by spray and/or large waves
Some delays to road, rail, air and ferry transport are likely
Probably some bus and train services affected, with some journeys taking longer
Delays for high-sided vehicles on exposed routes and bridges likely
Some loss of power and other services is possible

areas.name: North West England | Northern Ireland | South West England | Strathclyde | SW Scotland, Lothian Borders | Wales

warnings.headline: A spell of strong winds may lead to damaging gusts and transport disruption.: UPDATED
warnings.description: Information on update: Warning area adjusted northward and end time brought forwards. Strong west to southwesterly winds are expected to spread across much of Scotland and fringe the north of Northern Ireland during Tuesday. Gusts of 50-60 mph are possible quite widely and some coastal or exposed areas in the northwest and far north of Scotland could see gusts of 70 mph or more. There is still some uncertainty regarding the peak gusts, but the highest winds are expected in the far north and northwest and most likely over the Hebrides. The strongest of the winds will reduce from the southwest later on Tuesday, with the far north of Scotland the last to see winds ease.
impacts: There is a chance of longer journey times or cancellations as road, rail, air and ferry services are affected
There is a chance that some roads and bridges could close
There is a small chance that injuries and danger to life could occur from large waves and beach material being thrown onto sea fronts, coastal roads and properties
There is a slight chance of some damage to buildings, such as tiles blown from roofs, as well as damage to trees
There is a chance that power cuts may occur, with the potential to affect other services, such as mobile phone coverage
There is a small chance of injuries and danger to life from flying debris

warnings.description: Following heavy rain and strong winds over the weekend, river and lake levels remain above flood warning thresholds. Further rainfall and strong winds are expected. Locations most affected will be Keswick Campsite flooding from the lake and the River Greta. We continue to closely monitor the situation . Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water. This message will be updated by 9:00AM on Tuesday 27 October or as the situation changes.

warnings.event: Flood Warning: Poole Harbour at West Quay and Lower Hamworthy Quay
warnings.headline: Flooding is expected: Poole Harbour at West Quay and Lower Hamworthy Quay
warnings.description:
High tides are expected to cause flooding this evening. 

Flooding is expected from 07:11pm to 11:11pm on 26/10/2026. 

Further flooding is possible on the morning high tide on Tuesday 27th October from 07:30am to 11:30am. Areas most at risk include Lower Hamworthy and areas of Poole from Old Town, The Quay to Hunger Hill. The detailed tidal forecast for those who use it is for a peak level at Poole RNLI. The first forecast high water of 1.63mAODN is at 09:11pm 26/10/2026 with southerly force 6 winds. The second forecast high water is at 09:30am 27/10/2026 with a level of 1.42mAODN with westerly force 5 winds. (mAODN is height above average sea level.) 

We are closely monitoring the situation . 

Activate any flood protection products you may have. Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded. 

This message will be updated by 1:00PM on Tuesday 27 October or as the situation changes.

warnings.event: Flood Warning: South Hayling and South Eastoke seafront
warnings.headline: Flooding is expected: South Hayling and South Eastoke seafront
warnings.description:
High tides are expected to cause flooding over the next two days.
Flooding is expected for 2 hours either side of Monday evening's tide at 23:18 on 26/10/2026  
The weather increases tide table values by 0.15 m. The total forecast tide is 5.03 metres Chart Datum (2.30 mAOD) at Portsmouth. Strong Southerly Force 6 wind. South Hayling beach (towards Eastoke) has been affected by previous storms. Water could push further up the beach than normal. Property at Eastoke corner, near the nature reserve, and at Southwood Road may flood. Overtopping of splash walls along the beach front may flood gardens. Beach huts at West Beach, near the Inn on the beach may also be affected.
Tuesday's tide at 11:40 27/10/2026 is forecast to be 7 cm lower (2.23 mAOD).
We are liaising with emergency services and local authorities .
Activate any flood protection products you may have. Avoid South Hayling seafront. Shingle can be thrown by wind and waves.
This message will be updated by 4:00PM on Tuesday 27 October or as the situation changes.
